name: Rerun after partner fixes: investigate current behaviour and specify the work (spike)
description:
**This ticket is the investigation and the specification. The implementation lives in the tickets listed at the bottom.**

## What was asked

When a partner pushes fixes after we've sent review comments, the tool re-runs the review on the new commit. This was to check how well that actually works today and specify what to do about it.

## What we found

A re-run today is a full, stateless re-review — it replaces our own prior findings rather than comparing against them, so there is no new / still-open / fixed distinction anywhere in the pipeline, even though the parent RFC assumes one exists.

On top of that: a partner's reply on an existing discussion thread is read and surfaced to a reviewer, but the thread itself is never closed by the tool, round 2 never touches round 1's thread, and an unfixed finding gets re-posted as a near-duplicate in a separate thread.

We also checked whether this used to exist upstream. The original `st-addon-review` skill did have a rerun mechanism — it tagged every comment with a hidden marker and, on the next run, compared the old and new commit to classify each prior finding, with one hard rule: fixed may only follow from the code actually changing, never from simply not re-flagging it. That machinery was deliberately dropped when the skill was adapted into this platform, because the platform's own rule is that the skill never touches GitHub directly. The capability was not rebuilt anywhere else — dropping it left a real gap, not a considered replacement.

**Team decision:** build a rerun that takes prior rounds into account, along the same new / still-open / fixed shape, with the comparison living in the tool's own pipeline rather than back in the skill.

## Three things the investigation changed

**Four claims are wrong today, independent of the rerun.** The letter can tell a partner the pull request is clean while blockers from the previous round still stand; the completion notice can tell them "0 findings" in the same situation; the conclusion in the console and Slack can read "approve" over those same blockers; and the automatic send can fire on top of all of it. All four happen for any partner who pushes twice and need none of the rerun machinery, so they were split out into **CZ3TDR1-634** and ship first.

**Partners close discussion threads themselves, and we don't read that at all.** A finding whose thread the partner closes — with or without fixing anything — disappears from the pull request and nobody on our side learns. The catch: the natural trigger for noticing is a new commit, and a partner who closes a thread instead of fixing it is precisely the one who never pushes again. Hence a daily check as its own piece of work (**CZ3TDR1-665**).

**Three unrelated defects** were found along the way and are fixed separately in **CZ3TDR1-633**.

## Decisions that are promises to partners

- A finding is closed only by a real change in the code — never because we didn't find it again the second time.
- When a partner writes that something is fixed but pushes nothing, they always get an answer, but that alone never closes the finding.
- The same applies when a partner closes a thread themselves: it is a claim, not proof.
- A partner cannot force a new full review of an unchanged commit.
- Nothing is sent, closed or reopened without a reviewer approving that specific message.

## One limitation we cannot promise up front

Whether we are able to close a thread at all depends on the access each partner gave our bot, and we cannot tell in advance — posting comments needs only read access, so the fact that comments work today says nothing about closing. Where we can't, the partner gets a clear closing message and the thread stays visually open. That is a serviceable outcome, not a failure: partners close threads themselves anyway.

## Before anything reaches a partner

One round runs silently first — the classification is recorded and compared against what the reviewer actually decided. Partners see nothing in that round.

---

## Outcome of the spike

The full specification is in **https://github.com/shoptet/aidev-apps/pull/27** — one document, two batches, every claim about the current behaviour verified against the code rather than carried over from this investigation.

**Batch 1 — ships first, on its own:**

- **CZ3TDR1-634** — the four claims that are wrong today.

**Batch 2 — the rerun feature, in dependency order:**

1. **CZ3TDR1-660** — remember which findings we already sent, and where they live.
2. **CZ3TDR1-661** — work out whether a change in the code actually fixed a finding.
3. **CZ3TDR1-662** — classify every carried-over finding, once per round.
4. **CZ3TDR1-663** — stop posting the same finding twice; say in the letter what carried over.
5. **CZ3TDR1-664** — give the reviewer somewhere to act on it.

**Independent of that chain:**

- **CZ3TDR1-665** — notice a discussion the partner closed without fixing anything (daily).
- **CZ3TDR1-666** — answer a re-review on an unchanged commit instead of doing nothing.

**Deferred by design**, needing a separate decision after the silent round: making a rebase cheaper to process, and forcing a fresh pass on an unchanged commit.

**Done when:** the specification exists and is agreed, and the implementation is carved into tickets with their order settled. Both are true — this ticket is finished; progress now lives in the children above.
